stem: A recurring deposit account accumulates Rs 25,000. The bank compounds interest at 10% per annum. What was the present value (principal deposited as a lump sum) if the maturity was at the end of 4 years? [Given: (1.10)^4 = 1.4641]

per_option_rationale.rationale: Finding the present value is the inverse of compounding: divide the future amount by (1 + r)^n rather than multiplying the principal.
Rs 15,000 arises from mistakenly dividing 25000 by 1.10^4 and computing 25000/1.666 approximately, using an incorrect value for (1.10)^4 of 1.6667 instead of 1.4641.
Rs 17,500 = 25000 - 25000 x 0.10 x 3 subtracts three years of simple interest from the maturity value instead of dividing by the compound factor.
Rs 22,727.27 = 25000 / 1.10 applies the discount for only 1 year (n = 1) instead of 4 years, using the annual factor once.

explanation: P = A / (1 + r)^n = 25000 / 1.4641 = Rs 17,075.34 (to the nearest paisa).

explanation_sections.punchline: Finding the present value is the inverse of compounding: divide the future amount by (1 + r)^n rather than multiplying the principal.
explanation_sections.lesson: The same formula A = P x (1 + r)^n works in reverse: when A is known, isolate P by dividing. Never subtract interest to go backwards.
explanation_sections.timing: 85 seconds: divide 25000 by 1.4641. An approximate check: 17000 x 1.4641 = 24889, 17075 x 1.4641 ~25000. Trap is option 4 (only one year of discounting).
